newsitem.title: USA: VEPCO sees wire charge of $0.01/kwh or less.
newsitem.headline: VEPCO sees wire charge of $0.01/kwh or less.

text.p: Virginia Electric Power Co expects to have a Transition Cost Charge of $0.01 per kilowatt hour or less once competition is allowed in Virginia, spokesman Bill Byrd said.

In a filing made with the State Corporation Commission Monday, the Dominion Resources Inc subsidiary proposed the wire charge to recover the cost of power purchases from non-utility generators and nuclear power plant decommissioning from all users of its transmission system rather than just those buying their energy from VEPCO.
Byrd said regulatory assets will not be included.
Monday said the utility now has about $800 million of regulatory assets, $500 million of which it expects to recover through rates over the next five years.

The remaining $300 million includes amounts not under the jurisdiction of Virginia regulators, he said, noting most of this component is regulated by North Carolina and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.
The rest is related to deferred taxes which the company expects to offset over the next seven years and normal depreciation, Byrd said.
